In-scope processes.value: Initial notice at establishment of the customer relationship (new business issue), the annual notice run for every in-force customer, revised notice before any new disclosure practice takes effect, and opt-out notice for NPFI shared with nonaffiliated third parties outside the service-provider/joint-marketing and transaction-processing exceptions

In-scope systems.value: Policy admin issue events fire the initial notice and hold the in-force population for the 12-month annual notice cohort; fulfilment files and per-recipient delivery receipts return to the document management repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Privacy Notice Delivery Procedure - trigger matrix (initial at or before relationship establishment, annual within any 12 consecutive months, revised before the new practice starts), per-state wording variants, channel rules including E-SIGN consent, and proof-of-delivery capture

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Privacy Counsel and the Head of Compliance; re-approved annually before the annual notice run and re-opened on any department bulletin amending a state's Model 672 adoption

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Initial notice no later than the date the customer relationship is established; annual notice at least once in any period of 12 consecutive months while the relationship continues; revised notice delivered before NPFI moves under the new practice; 30-day reasonable opportunity to opt out before the first disclosure

Deadline reminders configured.value: Notice calendar fires T-60 / T-30 / T-7 before each anniversary cohort's 12-month annual notice due date, plus a same-day alert on any issued policy with no initial-notice delivery record within one business day of issue

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Counsel signs off every re-mailing plan, every notice wording change and any decision that a cohort does not need re-noticing

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on a missing initial notice; annual notice delivery of at least 99.5% of the due cohort with 100% of the shortfall re-mailed within 30 days; any jurisdiction served the wrong state variant is an outright fail

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Notice version library with effective dates, the per-jurisdiction variant matrix and delivery-proof extracts by policy number, producible to an Arizona DIFI market conduct examiner within 10 business days

checklist.step: Refresh the 51-jurisdiction notice requirements matrix
actions: Open the regulatory library entry for NAIC Model 672 and pull each state's adopting regulation, starting with Arizona (DIFI), Michigan and Oregon as the drafting benchmarks.

For each of the 51 jurisdictions record on the matrix row: initial notice trigger wording, annual notice requirement and whether the state recognises the federal annual-notice exception, opt-out method requirements, health-information opt-in requirement, and any state-mandated notice language.
Diff each row against last year's matrix and hand the Privacy Officer a list of changed jurisdictions with the bulletin or session law that caused the change.
Save a dated PDF capture of every amended state regulation as the source behind the matrix row.
checklist.done: all 51 matrix rows carry a current citation, a dated source capture and a changed/unchanged flag versus the prior year.

checklist.step: Map the notice triggers onto real policy admin events
actions: With the Policy Admin Ops Lead, list every event that establishes a customer relationship: new business issue, reinstatement after lapse, assumption or novation of a book, and term conversion.
For each event name the exact policy admin status transition and the field that carries the relationship start date.
Confirm with Underwriting Operations that quote-only and declined applications are excluded because no customer relationship is created, and write that decision and its basis onto the map.
Publish the trigger map to the Privacy Officer and the fulfilment configuration team as the specification for the issue-time notice.
checklist.done: every relationship-establishing event maps to a named status transition and a dated field, with exclusions written down and justified.

checklist.step: Refresh the notice text and the categories it discloses
actions: Reconcile the notice's 'information we collect' and 'information we share' sections line by line to the current processing register so the notice describes what actually happens.
Ask Underwriting, Claims, Marketing and Distribution to confirm in writing every category of nonaffiliated third party they send NPFI to and the purpose of each.
Rewrite any category the business could not evidence and add any sharing found in the register but missing from the notice.
Stamp the draft with a version number and effective date and route it to Privacy Counsel.
checklist.done: the draft notice's collection and sharing categories reconcile to the processing register with written business confirmations attached.

checklist.step: Produce and approve the per-state notice variants
actions: Apply each matrix row's state-specific requirements to the base notice to produce the variant set, including state-mandated headings and opt-out language.
Where a state requires health-information authorization language, insert the opt-in wording instead of the opt-out wording and mark the variant NPHI.
Mark each variant approved with counsel name, date and version number, then lock the file against edits.
Hand the approved variant set to the Content Specialist for production with the effective date stated.
checklist.done: one counsel-approved, version-stamped variant exists per jurisdiction, with NPHI variants flagged separately.

checklist.step: Produce the print and electronic renditions and prove they are readable
actions: Typeset each approved variant into the print rendition and the HTML/PDF e-delivery rendition without changing a word of approved text.
Check the rendition against the clear-and-conspicuous requirement: minimum body point size, headings intact, opt-out instructions not buried in a footnote.
Run a side-by-side text diff of the rendition against the counsel-locked source and fix any drift before release.
Load the final renditions into the document repository under the version number and effective date and mark prior versions superseded.
checklist.done: every variant exists as a print and an electronic rendition that diffs clean against the counsel-approved text.

checklist.step: Configure the initial notice to fire at relationship establishment
actions: Wire the notice job to each status transition on the trigger map so the notice queues no later than the issue date, not the first billing date.
Select the variant from the policyholder's mailing-address state, not the writing company's state of domicile.
Set the fulfilment record to write back a delivery record carrying policy number, variant id, channel and dispatch date.
Run the configuration over a 100-policy multi-state batch in the test environment and confirm every policy drew the right variant before promoting.
checklist.done: issue-time notices queue on the issue date with the correct state variant and a write-back delivery record, proven on a multi-state test batch.

checklist.step: Build the annual notice cohort for the 12-month window
actions: Extract every customer with a continuing relationship together with the date of their last delivered privacy notice.
Select everyone whose last notice date is approaching 12 consecutive months and confirm the cohort spans all writing companies and product lines.
Reconcile the cohort count to the in-force policy count from the policy admin platform and investigate any difference over 0.5% before releasing the file.
Deduplicate to household or customer level using the documented dedup rule and record how many records collapsed.
checklist.done: the annual cohort is extracted, reconciled to in-force counts within tolerance, deduplicated by a documented rule and signed by the extractor.

checklist.step: Gate electronic delivery behind valid E-SIGN consent
actions: Pull the e-delivery consent table and keep only customers with an affirmative, unrevoked consent and a validated email address.
Move anyone whose consent was revoked, whose email hard-bounced last cycle, or who never consented back onto the print channel.
Confirm the portal posts the notice to the customer document centre as well as emailing it, so the notice is retrievable after the email is deleted.
Return the e-delivery versus print volume split to the Privacy Officer before the run is released.
checklist.done: the e-delivery list holds only affirmative unrevoked consents with deliverable addresses and everyone else is routed to print.

checklist.step: Release the files to fulfilment and reconcile the counts
actions: Transmit the print file and the e-delivery file to the fulfilment vendor with the variant mapping and the required in-home date.
Reconcile the vendor's acknowledgement counts back to the cohort file by state and variant and clear any difference the same day.
Collect the vendor's dispatch confirmation, postal manifest and email send log and store them against the notice version.
Refuse to close the run until the vendor supplies a per-record disposition file rather than a batch total.
checklist.done: vendor acknowledgement, dispatch manifest and per-record disposition file all reconcile to the released cohort by state and variant.

checklist.step: Work undeliverables and re-mail
actions: Load the returned-mail and email hard-bounce file and match each record back to its policy.
Run returned addresses through the address-correction service and, where a better address is found, re-mail within 10 business days.
Where no address can be found, record the record as undeliverable after reasonable effort with the steps attempted and their dates.
Report the residual undeliverable count and rate to the Privacy Officer at the close of the run.
checklist.done: every undeliverable is either re-mailed to a corrected address or documented as undeliverable after named, dated attempts.

checklist.step: Deliver the opt-out notice and hold the 30-day opportunity open
actions: For every disclosure of NPFI to a nonaffiliated third party that does not sit inside the service-provider/joint-marketing or transaction-processing exceptions, include the opt-out notice and the opt-out means with the privacy notice.
Offer at least two simple opt-out methods - the toll-free number and the reply form or portal switch - and confirm both are live before the file is released.
Suppress the affected records from any disclosure to that third party until 30 days after the dispatch date, and hold the suppression permanently for anyone who opts out.
Log the dispatch date, the 30-day expiry date and the third party each cohort was suppressed from.
checklist.done: no NPFI reached a nonaffiliated third party before the 30-day opportunity expired, and the suppression window is logged per cohort and third party.

checklist.step: Issue a revised notice before any new disclosure practice starts
actions: Take intake from the change advisory process for any new data sharing, new third party or new purpose touching NPFI or NPHI.
Decide whether the current notice already covers it; where it does not, draft the revised notice and a fresh opt-out notice.
Set the earliest permitted disclosure date at 30 days after revised-notice dispatch and hand that date to the receiving business area as a hard gate.
Hold the change until the revised notice is dispatched - starting the sharing first is not an available option.
checklist.done: every new or changed NPFI disclosure has a dispatched revised notice and a dated earliest-disclosure gate before any data moves.

checklist.step: Push the current notice and opt-out means through the producer channel
actions: Publish the current notice variants and effective date to the portal forms library and retire the superseded versions the same day.
Send a channel bulletin stating the version number, the effective date and that superseded notices must not be handed to applicants.
Confirm the point-of-sale application packet build now pulls the current variant and spot-check three agency packets per state region.
Track producer acknowledgements and chase any agency that has not acknowledged within 15 business days.
checklist.done: the portal serves only current variants, superseded versions are withdrawn, and producer acknowledgements are tracked to closure.

checklist.step: File the notice evidence under retention
actions: File per notice version: the counsel-approved text, both renditions, the cohort file, the vendor dispatch manifest, the per-record disposition file and the undeliverable log.
Apply the six-years-after-relationship-termination retention label so the record survives policy lapse.
Confirm the repository index makes the record retrievable by policy number, jurisdiction, notice version and dispatch date.
Test retrieval on five random policy numbers across three states and record the result in the run file.
checklist.done: the notice evidence set is filed, retention-labelled and proven retrievable by policy number and jurisdiction on a documented spot test.

checklist.step: Log and remediate every notice exception
actions: Raise an exception for each missed initial notice, each annual notice past the 12-month window, each wrong-variant delivery and each unresolved undeliverable cohort.
Record cohort size, jurisdictions affected, root cause (trigger not fired, cohort query gap, stale variant, address quality) and an accountable owner.
Set the remediation mailing date and confirm the re-mail happened by tracing to the vendor disposition file.
Escalate any exception touching more than 500 customers to the Head of Compliance within one business day.
checklist.done: every notice exception carries a cohort size, root cause, owner, completed remediation mailing and a disposition.

testing.step: Build the population of notice-triggering events for the period
actions: Extract from the policy admin issue log every new business issue, reinstatement, conversion and assumed policy with a relationship start date inside the period, by writing company and state.
Extract separately every in-force customer whose 12-month annual notice window closed inside the period.
Reconcile both extracts to the new-business and in-force counts in monthly production reporting and clear differences before sampling.
Have the extractor sign the population as complete and record the query text and run date in the workpaper.
testing.done: both populations reconcile to production reporting and are signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to delivered notices in the fulfilment record
actions: Match every population record to a delivery record on policy number plus dispatch date.
Check the initial notice dispatch date is on or before the relationship start date and the annual dispatch falls inside the 12-consecutive-month window.
List unmatched records and late dispatches as automatic exceptions with no judgement applied.
Quantify the unmatched population by state so jurisdictional exposure is visible to the Privacy Officer.
testing.done: every population record is matched to a timely delivery record or listed as an exception with its jurisdiction.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of records in jurisdictions whose Model 672 adoption carries state-mandated notice language.
Take 40 records at random with a recorded seed from the remaining population, stratified so no single state contributes more than 10.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Add every prior-period open exception as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all mandated-language states and carries forward prior open exceptions.

testing.step: Re-perform the variant selection against the jurisdiction matrix
actions: For each sampled record read the policyholder's mailing-address state from policy admin, then look up the required variant in the jurisdiction matrix before opening the delivered document.
Compare your conclusion to the variant actually delivered; the right notice reached under the wrong rule still counts as an exception.
Check the delivered version's effective date was current on the dispatch date and not a superseded edition.
Capture the matrix row and the delivered document image into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled record has an independent variant conclusion, a version-currency check and captured evidence.

testing.step: Inspect each delivered document against the content requirements
actions: Open the archived image of each sampled notice and confirm it states the categories of information collected, the categories disclosed, the categories of nonaffiliated third parties, and the confidentiality and security practices.
Confirm the opt-out notice, where required for that record, names at least two simple opt-out methods and states the 30-day opportunity.
Confirm NPHI records received the opt-in authorization wording rather than opt-out wording.
Treat a missing element as a content failure and name which element was absent.
testing.done: every sampled notice is inspected element by element with any missing element named.

testing.step: Verify the E-SIGN consent behind every electronically delivered notice
actions: For each e-delivered sample record open the consent record and check it is affirmative, dated before dispatch and unrevoked at the dispatch date.
Confirm the email send log shows a successful delivery rather than a bounce, and that the document was also posted to the customer document centre.
Where consent is missing or revoked, treat the notice as undelivered and check whether a print notice followed.
Capture the consent record and the send-log entry into the workpaper.
testing.done: every e-delivered sample has a valid unrevoked consent and a successful delivery, or is logged as undelivered.

testing.step: Recompute the 12-month interval and the 30-day opt-out window
actions: For 15 sampled annual notice records recompute the interval between the prior and current dispatch dates and confirm it does not exceed 12 consecutive months.
For every sampled record carrying an opt-out notice recompute dispatch date plus 30 days and compare it to the first date NPFI was actually released to the named third party.
Pull the third-party disclosure extract for those records and confirm no release occurred inside the window.
Treat any release inside the 30-day window as a reportable breach of the obligation, not a test exception.
testing.done: no sampled annual notice exceeded 12 months and no disclosure occurred before the 30-day opportunity expired.

testing.step: Trace opt-out elections through to downstream suppression
actions: Pull every opt-out election received in the period across the toll-free, reply-form and portal channels.
For 25 elections check the suppression flag is set on the customer record and that the flag date is inside the documented propagation SLA from the election date.
Query the outbound third-party disclosure extracts dated after the flag and confirm none of the 25 appears.
Log any customer whose data moved after opting out with the third party, the date and the record count.
testing.done: every tested opt-out is flagged within SLA and absent from every downstream disclosure extract after the flag date.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying policy number or cohort id, jurisdiction, the element that failed and the consumer impact.
Assign a root cause from the standing list - trigger not fired, cohort query gap, superseded variant served, consent not validated, suppression not propagated - and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date, and for any disclosure made before the opt-out window closed open a self-report assessment with Privacy Counsel.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the initial-notice failure count and the annual-notice delivery rate and compare them to the zero-tolerance and 99.5% thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with the workpaper references that support it.
Have the Internal Auditor, who sits outside the Privacy Office and built none of the notice files, sign the workpaper.
Report the result, open breaches and any self-report decision to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper under the test period.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, measured delivery rate and a committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Publish every intake channel and route them all into one queue
actions: Confirm the toll-free privacy number, the portal 'Your privacy choices' form, the privacy mailbox and the postal address printed on the privacy notice are all live and monitored daily.
Set the contact centre disposition codes for privacy opt-out, access request, correction request and authorization revocation so agents cannot close a rights call as a general enquiry.
Route each disposition and each inbound mailbox item straight into the rights case queue rather than the general correspondence queue.
Test each channel end to end once a month by submitting a seeded request and confirming a case is created with the correct type.
checklist.done: all four intake channels are live, dispositioned and proven by a seeded monthly test to open a correctly typed case.

checklist.step: Open the case and start the SLA clock on the receipt date
actions: Create the case with requester name, policy or claim number, jurisdiction of residence, channel, and the postmark or system timestamp as the receipt date.
Classify the request as opt-out, access, correction/amendment/deletion, or authorization revocation - split a mixed request into separate cases so each carries its own clock.
Set the due date at receipt plus 30 business days for access and correction cases and same-day for opt-outs and revocations.
Never restart the clock because the file was reassigned or the requester was chased for detail.
checklist.done: each request has a case with a classification, jurisdiction and a due date computed from the original receipt date.

checklist.step: Verify the requester's identity before anything is disclosed
actions: Match at least three data points against the policy record - full name, date of birth, policy number and either the last four of the government id on file or the mailing address of record.
For a request made by an attorney, executor or guardian, obtain the letter of authority, letters testamentary or power of attorney and file it on the case.
Where verification fails, write to the address of record, not the address on the request, asking for the missing proof and record that the clock keeps running.
Record the verification method, the data points matched and the verifier's name on the case before any search begins.
checklist.done: identity is verified on named, recorded data points or documented authority, with the verification note on the case before any search runs.

checklist.step: Search every system that holds the requester's recorded personal information
actions: Resolve the requester to a single customer id in the MDM hub and pull every linked party, policy, claim and quote id.
Run the standing search list against policy admin, the claims platform, billing, CRM, the contact centre recording archive, the underwriting workstation and the document repository.
Include information the company obtained from consumer reporting agencies and other outside sources, and identify each source so it can be named in the response.
Record per system whether records were found, the record count and the extract file name on the case.
checklist.done: every system on the standing search list returns a found/not-found result with counts, and outside sources are named.

checklist.step: Apply the permitted withholdings and mark them on the file
actions: Review the extract and withhold only what the statute permits - information collected in connection with a claim or civil or criminal proceeding, and material subject to legal privilege.
For medical record information, apply the state's rule on disclosure through the requester's designated medical professional where the state requires it.
Record the withholding basis and citation for each withheld item rather than a blanket redaction note.
Sign the withholding decision so the reasons letter can quote it verbatim.
checklist.done: each withheld item carries a named statutory basis and a counsel signature, with no blanket redactions.

checklist.step: Draft and issue the access response inside 30 business days
actions: Assemble the response pack: the recorded personal information, the identity of the sources it came from, and the identity of anyone to whom it was disclosed in the preceding period the statute names.
Include the statement of the requester's right to seek correction, amendment or deletion and how to exercise it.
Send by the channel the requester asked for, defaulting to the address of record, and capture the dispatch date and tracking reference on the case.
Where information is withheld, attach the reasons letter naming the statutory ground for each withheld category.
checklist.done: the response pack, source list, disclosure list and correction-rights statement are dispatched with a captured date inside 30 business days.

checklist.step: Decide correction, amendment and deletion requests and notify onward recipients
actions: Compare the disputed item to the underlying source document and decide to correct, amend, delete or refuse within 30 business days of receipt.
Where corrected, update the record in the system of record and push the correction to every downstream system on the lineage map.
Notify any person or entity to whom the incorrect information was disclosed in the statutory look-back period, plus any consumer reporting agency or insurance-support organisation that received it.
Where refused, issue the written reasons and record the requester's right to file a statement of disagreement, and file that statement with the record if supplied.
checklist.done: each correction request is decided in 30 business days, propagated downstream, notified to prior recipients, or refused in writing with the disagreement right stated.

checklist.step: Apply opt-out elections and authorization revocations on receipt
actions: Set the NPFI sharing opt-out flag and, for health information, the withdrawn-authorization flag on the master customer record the day the election is received.
Confirm the flag replicates to policy admin, the marketing platform and every scheduled third-party extract within 5 business days.
Notify each nonaffiliated third party already receiving that customer's NPFI to stop, and record the notification date and recipient.
Treat the opt-out as continuing until revoked in writing by the customer - never time-limit it or reset it at renewal.
checklist.done: the opt-out or revocation is flagged the day it arrives, replicated within 5 business days and notified to every current recipient.

checklist.step: Stop the downstream flows the election covers
actions: Confirm every scheduled outbound extract to a nonaffiliated third party joins to the suppression flag in its filter, not in a downstream report.
Re-run the last dispatched extract against the current suppression list and count any record that should have been excluded.
Where a suppressed record was already sent, raise a disclosure incident and instruct the recipient in writing to delete it, keeping the recipient's confirmation.
Add a pipeline test that fails the job when the suppression join is missing.
checklist.done: every outbound third-party extract filters on the live suppression flag and a failing pipeline test guards the join.

checklist.step: Handle requests that arrive through producers and brokers
actions: Instruct agencies through the portal bulletin to forward any privacy request to the privacy mailbox within one business day of receipt and to keep the dated envelope or email.
Record on the case the date the producer received the request, not the date the company received it, because the SLA runs from the earlier date.
Chase any agency that forwards a request more than one business day late and log the delay against the agency.
Report repeat late-forwarding agencies to the Agency Relations Manager each quarter.
checklist.done: producer-received requests are cased against the producer receipt date and late-forwarding agencies are logged and reported.

checklist.step: Work the aged-case report before anything breaches
actions: Run the open-case report daily sorted by business days elapsed and jurisdiction.
Escalate cases at day 15 to the Privacy Ops lead, day 22 to the DPO and day 27 to the Head of Compliance with a named blocker for each.
For any case that will breach, get the response out with a partial answer and a follow-up commitment rather than waiting for completeness.
Record the blocker cause on each escalated case so the pattern is visible at quarter end.
checklist.done: no case reaches day 30 unescalated and every escalation carries a named blocker and cause.

checklist.step: Answer department complaints about rights requests on the department's clock
actions: Link any ALDOI or other department complaint to the underlying rights case and pull the full case history.
Draft the department response setting out the receipt date, the actions taken with dates and the outcome, attaching the response letter actually sent.
Have Privacy Counsel clear the draft before it is filed with the department, especially where the response concedes a late answer.
File the department response and its acknowledgement on both the complaint record and the rights case.
checklist.done: each department complaint is answered within the department's window from the linked case history, counsel-cleared and filed on both records.

checklist.step: Close the case and file the evidence
actions: File on closure: intake record, identity verification note, per-system search results, the response pack, the reasons letter and any downstream notification confirmations.
Apply the six-years-from-closure retention label and link the record to the customer id so it surfaces on any later request.
Confirm the case cannot be closed in the tool without a dispatch date and a response artefact attached.
Spot-check five closed cases a month for a missing artefact and reopen any that fail.
checklist.done: closure is blocked without a dispatch date and response artefact, and the filed record is retention-labelled and linked to the customer.

checklist.step: Report rights volumes, SLA performance and themes monthly
actions: Publish a monthly dashboard of requests received by type, channel and jurisdiction, cases closed within 30 business days, average elapsed days and open aged cases.
Break out opt-out volumes by acquisition source so a spike from one campaign is visible.
Present themes and the top three root causes of delay to the Head of Compliance with named owners.
Feed any recurring source-system search gap to the Data Governance Lead for the standing search list.
checklist.done: a monthly dashboard with SLA performance, opt-out volumes and named delay owners is issued to the Head of Compliance.

checklist.step: Log and remediate every rights exception
actions: Raise an exception for each case answered after 30 business days, each disclosure made to an unverified requester and each opt-out not propagated within 5 business days.
Record days late, jurisdiction, root cause and an accountable owner, and issue an apology and corrected response to the affected consumer.
Where an unverified disclosure occurred, run it through the incident process as a potential unauthorised disclosure.
Track the remediation to closure and retest the same control the following quarter.
checklist.done: every late, unverified or unpropagated case has an exception with days late, root cause, owner, consumer remedy and a retest.

testing.step: Build the population of rights requests received in the quarter
actions: Extract every rights case with a receipt date in the quarter with request type, jurisdiction, channel, receipt date, response date and outcome.
Separately extract contact centre privacy dispositions, portal privacy-choice submissions and privacy mailbox items for the same period.
Reconcile the channel extracts to the case log and treat any channel item with no case as a completeness failure before sampling.
Have the extractor sign the reconciled population and record the queries in the workpaper.
testing.done: the case population is reconciled to all four intake channels with unmatched channel items listed as completeness failures.

testing.step: Reconcile the case log to the systems of record for opt-out flags
actions: Pull every customer record carrying an NPFI opt-out or withdrawn-authorization flag set during the quarter.
Match each flag back to a rights case; a flag with no case, or a case with no flag, is an exception on its face.
Compare the flag date to the case receipt date and compute the propagation lag in business days.
List every unmatched record by jurisdiction for the sampling step.
testing.done: every opt-out flag ties to a case and every opt-out case ties to a flag, with propagation lag computed.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of cases that breached 30 business days and 100% of cases where access was refused in whole or part.
Take 30 further cases at random with a recorded seed, stratified across access, correction, opt-out and revocation types.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every prior-quarter open exception as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample covers all breaches and refusals, is stratified by request type and is reproducible from a recorded seed.

testing.step: Re-perform identity verification on the sample
actions: For each sampled case read the verification note and independently match the recorded data points against the policy record.
Confirm at least three data points matched, or that documented authority was on file for a representative request.
Check nothing was disclosed before the verification date recorded on the case.
Treat any disclosure preceding verification as a control failure and route it to the incident process.
testing.done: each sampled case shows three matched data points or filed authority, with no disclosure before the verification date.

testing.step: Re-run the source-system search for a subset and test completeness
actions: For 10 sampled access cases resolve the requester in the MDM hub yourself and list every linked party, policy, claim and quote id.
Search the standing list of systems independently and compare your record counts to the counts recorded on the case.
Investigate any system the case shows as not searched and confirm whether it genuinely held nothing.
Capture your search output alongside the case extract in the workpaper.
testing.done: independently re-run searches reconcile to the case record counts, or the difference is documented as an exception.

testing.step: Recompute the SLA clock on every sampled case
actions: Recompute elapsed business days from the original receipt date - producer receipt date where applicable - to the dispatch date, excluding weekends and state holidays.
Compare your figure to the elapsed days the case reports and investigate any case where the tool's clock was reset or paused.
Confirm no case treated a chase for further detail as a clock stop.
List every case over 30 business days with the recomputed overrun.
testing.done: elapsed days are independently recomputed on every sampled case and every clock reset is investigated.

testing.step: Test the content of the response letters and refusals
actions: Read each sampled response and confirm it discloses the recorded personal information, names the sources it came from and lists prior disclosure recipients where the statute requires.
Confirm the correction-rights statement is present and legible in every access response.
For each refusal check the letter names the statutory ground, is signed by counsel and states the right to file a statement of disagreement.
Treat a refusal supported only by a general 'not required' as a fail, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every sampled response contains the required elements and every refusal names a verified statutory ground.

testing.step: Prove suppression held in the outbound third-party extracts
actions: List every outbound extract sent to a nonaffiliated third party in the quarter with its run date and record count.
Join each extract to the opt-out population and identify any suppressed customer that still appears after the flag date.
For any hit, retrieve the recipient's deletion confirmation and the incident record.
Compute the suppression propagation rate within 5 and within 10 business days and compare to the 99% and 100% thresholds.
testing.done: no suppressed customer appears in a post-flag extract without a logged incident, and propagation rates are measured against threshold.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception carrying case id, jurisdiction, request type, days late or element failed, and the consumer impact.
Assign a root cause from the standing list - channel not cased, verification skipped, system omitted from search, clock reset, suppression join missing - and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where a consumer was harmed by a late or refused response, require a corrected response and a written apology.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date, consumer remedy where relevant and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time response rate, the unverified-disclosure count and the suppression propagation rates and compare each to its threshold.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the Compliance Officer, who handled and approved none of the sampled cases, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any department complaint exposure to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper under the quarter.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, measured on-time rate and a committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Data Protection Officer and endorsed by the Data Governance Council; re-approved annually and whenever a state amends its Model 672 adoption or the notice text changes

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Register is continuous - new or changed activity registered before processing starts, steward attestation each quarter, full register reconciliation to the privacy notice before the annual notice run, and register refresh within 30 days of any system go-live

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Unregistered processing found in discovery, stale entries, and any disclosure with no recorded basis are logged as register exceptions with the activity, owner, remediation date and disposition

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero NPFI/NPHI-tagged system or third-party interface without a register entry; 100% steward attestation completed; every disclosure entry names a specific statutory basis - a blank or generic basis field is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous, so completeness discovery runs quarterly against the attestation cycle and a full register-to-notice reconciliation runs annually before the notice refresh

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly register completeness workpaper - discovery extracts, unmatched asset list, sampled entries, re-performed lineage traces and exceptions - in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Register export by jurisdiction showing purpose, data categories, recipients, disclosure basis and retention, tied to the privacy notice version in force, producible to ALDOI within 10 business days

checklist.step: Fix what counts as a registrable processing activity
actions: Write the unit of registration: a purpose plus a data category plus a system, so 'underwriting risk assessment - NPFI credit-based insurance score - underwriting workstation' is one entry, not three.

List the mandatory fields every entry must carry: purpose, NPFI/NPHI categories, source, systems, internal and external recipients, disclosure basis relied on, retention period, jurisdictions and the accountable steward.
Agree with the Data Governance Council which business areas each steward covers so no system is ownerless.
Publish the definition and field list to all stewards before the first collection round opens.
checklist.done: the registration unit, mandatory fields and steward-to-area mapping are published and acknowledged by every steward.

checklist.step: Tag the NPFI and NPHI elements in the catalog
actions: Load the element list that constitutes nonpublic personal financial information - name tied to a policy, account and payment details, premium and claim amounts, credit-based scores, driving and loss history - and tag those columns in the catalog.
Tag health information separately as NPHI so the opt-in authorization rule can be enforced on it.
Run the classification scanner over policy admin, claims, billing, CRM and the warehouse and review the machine-proposed tags with each steward.
Publish the tagged asset list as the discovery baseline for register completeness.
checklist.done: NPFI and NPHI columns are tagged and steward-reviewed across every core system, producing a published discovery baseline.

checklist.step: Collect register entries from each business area
actions: For each tagged asset in your area describe the processing purpose in business language a consumer would recognise, not the project name.
Name the internal recipients and every nonaffiliated third party the data reaches, with the interface or file that carries it.
State the retention period actually applied in the system, and where it differs from the retention schedule, say so rather than copying the schedule.
Submit the entry to the Privacy Office with the system owner and the interface owner both named.
checklist.done: each tagged asset in the area has a submitted entry with a consumer-recognisable purpose, named recipients and the retention actually applied.

checklist.step: Record the disclosure basis for every external recipient
actions: For each nonaffiliated third-party recipient pick the basis: consent or authorization, the service-provider and joint-marketing exception with its contractual confidentiality clause, or a transaction-processing/ordinary-business exception - and cite the article of the state adoption.
For NPHI recipients require a signed authorization and record its form id, scope and expiry rather than relying on an opt-out.
Where no basis holds, mark the flow as unlawful pending remediation and hand it to the Privacy Officer as a stop item, not a finding.
Sign each recorded basis so the entry shows counsel name and date.
checklist.done: every external recipient carries a cited, counsel-signed basis or is marked unlawful pending remediation.

checklist.step: Trace lineage so the register matches how data actually moves
actions: Pull the lineage graph for each tagged column from source system through the warehouse to every consuming mart, report and outbound extract.
Compare the graph to the recipients listed on the register entry and list any consumer the steward did not declare.
Check whether any downstream copy strips the NPFI tag, and re-tag it so classification travels with the data.
Return the undeclared-consumer list to the owning steward with a 10 business day correction window.
checklist.done: each entry's recipient list reconciles to the lineage graph and every downstream copy carries the classification tag.

checklist.step: Reconcile the register to the privacy notice
actions: Roll the register's data categories and recipient categories up to the wording used in the privacy notice.
List anything shared in the register but not described in the notice - that gap needs a revised notice before the sharing continues.
List anything described in the notice but absent from the register - that is either dead wording to remove or unregistered processing to find.
Hand both lists to Privacy Counsel before the annual notice text is locked.
checklist.done: both directions of the register-to-notice reconciliation are documented and cleared before the notice text is locked.

checklist.step: Record retention and disposal per entry
actions: Map each entry to its records schedule class and state the trigger event - policy termination, claim closure, last customer contact - not just a number of years.
Confirm with the system owner that an automated purge or archive job actually enforces that period, and name the job.
Where no purge job exists, record the entry as retention-unenforced and raise it for remediation with a target date.
Note any legal hold that suspends disposal and the matter it belongs to.
checklist.done: every entry names a retention trigger, the enforcing purge job or its absence, and any active legal hold.

checklist.step: Register cross-border and affiliate flows separately
actions: List every flow of NPFI to an affiliate, an offshore service centre or a cloud region outside the United States, with the country and the entity.
Record the safeguard relied on - intra-group agreement, standard contractual clauses, or the vendor's data processing addendum - and its execution date.
Confirm the privacy notice's affiliate-sharing description covers what the flow actually does.
Flag any offshore flow with no executed safeguard to the Third-Party Risk Manager the day it is found.
checklist.done: every affiliate and offshore flow is registered with a named, dated safeguard or flagged to Third-Party Risk.

checklist.step: Gate new processing through register intake
actions: Add a mandatory privacy question set to the change and project intake form: does this touch NPFI or NPHI, what purpose, which recipients, what retention.
Route any 'yes' to the Privacy Office for a register entry before the build starts, and record the entry id on the change ticket.
Block go-live approval where the register entry id field is empty.
Report monthly on changes that reached go-live without an entry id and the approver who released them.
checklist.done: no change touching NPFI reaches go-live without a register entry id on the ticket, and bypasses are reported monthly.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly steward attestation
actions: Open the attestation task 15 days before quarter end and review each of your entries field by field.
Confirm, amend or retire each entry, giving a reason for every retirement rather than deleting the row.
Attest that no NPFI processing in your area is missing from the register, naming any you added this quarter.
Submit before the quarter-end due date; unattested entries are reported to the Data Governance Council by name.
checklist.done: every entry is confirmed, amended or retired with reasons, and each steward's attestation is submitted and dated.

checklist.step: Hunt for unregistered processing
actions: Take the tagged-asset discovery baseline and left-join it to the register on system and data category.
List every tagged asset with no register entry and every production outbound interface with no matching entry.
Chase each unmatched item to a named steward with a 15 business day window to register or justify.
Escalate anything still unmatched after the window to the DPO as an unregistered-processing exception.
checklist.done: the tagged-asset and interface baselines fully reconcile to the register, or the residue is escalated as exceptions.

checklist.step: Release and version the quarterly register
actions: Freeze the register at quarter end and export a dated snapshot with entry count, attestation coverage and open exceptions.
Sign the release note stating what changed since the prior snapshot and which entries were added, amended or retired.
File the snapshot with the six-year retention label so the register as at any past date can be reproduced.
Circulate the release note to the Head of Compliance and the Data Governance Council.
checklist.done: a dated, signed register snapshot with a change summary is filed under retention each quarter.

checklist.step: Feed the register into vendor, assessment and incident work
actions: Push the recipient list to the Third-Party Risk Manager so every registered external recipient has a contract with the confidentiality and use-limitation clauses.
Push high-risk entries - NPHI, credit-based scoring, automated decisioning, offshore processing - to the assessment queue.
Give the Incident Response Lead the register's system-to-data-category map so a breach can be scoped by data category within hours.
Confirm each downstream consumer acknowledges the feed each quarter.
checklist.done: the recipient list, high-risk queue and incident scoping map are all fed from the register and acknowledged by their owners.

checklist.step: Report register health to governance
actions: Publish a quarterly dashboard: entries by business area, attestation completion rate, stale entries over 12 months, entries with no cited disclosure basis and unregistered-processing exceptions.
Show the trend across four quarters so a deteriorating area is visible rather than a single-quarter number.
Name the accountable steward against each red metric.
Table the dashboard at the Data Governance Council and record the actions agreed.
checklist.done: a quarterly register-health dashboard with named owners is tabled at the Council and its actions minuted.

checklist.step: Log and remediate register exceptions
actions: Raise an exception for each unregistered processing activity, each entry with a blank disclosure basis and each missed attestation.
Record the business area, the data categories at risk, the root cause and an accountable owner.
For any flow marked unlawful pending remediation, agree a stop-or-fix date with the DPO and suspend the flow if the date passes.
Retest every remediated exception in the following quarter's completeness run.
checklist.done: every register exception has an owner, root cause, a stop-or-fix date where the flow lacks a basis, and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Build the register and discovery populations
actions: Export the frozen quarter-end register snapshot with every field and the entry change history.
Independently extract the discovery baseline: catalog assets tagged NPFI or NPHI, the production system inventory and the list of live outbound third-party interfaces.
Reconcile the discovery counts to the system inventory owned by IT so the baseline itself is complete.
Record both extracts, their queries and run dates in the workpaper and have the extractor sign them.
testing.done: the register snapshot and an independently built discovery baseline are extracted, reconciled to the IT inventory and signed.

testing.step: Reconcile discovery to the register and quantify the gap
actions: Join the discovery baseline to the register on system plus data category and list every unmatched tagged asset.
Join the outbound interface list to the register recipients and list every interface with no registered recipient.
Classify each gap as unregistered processing, mis-keyed entry or retired system and confirm the classification with the steward.
Report the gap count against the zero-tolerance threshold before sampling.
testing.done: every tagged asset and outbound interface is matched to a register entry or classified as a gap with steward confirmation.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of entries covering NPHI, credit-based scoring, offshore processing and any flow marked unlawful pending remediation.
Take 30 further entries at random with a recorded seed, stratified so each business area contributes at least three.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every prior-quarter open register exception as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample covers all high-risk entries, is stratified across business areas and is reproducible from a recorded seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the disclosure basis call on the sample
actions: For each sampled external recipient read the Alabama adoption article cited and decide independently whether the exception genuinely covers the flow.
Where the service-provider or joint-marketing exception is claimed, require the contract clause that limits use to the disclosed purpose and check it exists.
For NPHI recipients confirm a signed authorization exists, is in scope and has not expired.
Treat a right answer resting on the wrong article as an exception, and a blank basis as a fail.
testing.done: each sampled recipient has an independent basis conclusion supported by the contract clause or authorization it relies on.

testing.step: Trace three entries end to end through lineage
actions: Pick three sampled entries and pull the lineage for their tagged columns from source through the warehouse to every consumer.
Compare the consumers found to the recipients declared on the entry and list any undeclared consumer.
Check the classification tag persists on every downstream copy rather than being dropped at a transformation.
Capture the lineage graph into the workpaper as evidence of the trace.
testing.done: three end-to-end traces are captured, with any undeclared consumer or dropped classification tag listed.

testing.step: Test the register against the privacy notice in force
actions: Take the privacy notice version in force at quarter end and list its stated collection and sharing categories.
Map every sampled register entry to a notice category and list any sharing the notice does not describe.
Confirm anything the notice does not cover was either stopped or covered by a dispatched revised notice with a date.
Escalate any live sharing outside the notice immediately rather than holding it for the report.
testing.done: every sampled sharing maps to notice wording, or is proven stopped or covered by a dated revised notice.

testing.step: Recompute retention and prove disposal runs
actions: For 10 sampled entries recompute the disposal due date from the stated trigger event plus the retention period.
Query the system for records past that date and count what should have been purged but is still present.
Confirm the named purge job ran on schedule by reading its last run log, and check any legal hold covering the residue.
Report the over-retained record count by entry and business area.
testing.done: recomputed disposal dates are tested against live data, with the over-retained count and purge-job evidence recorded.

testing.step: Test the change-intake gate for new processing
actions: Extract every change that went live in the quarter and filter to those answering yes to the NPFI/NPHI intake question.
Check each one carries a register entry id and that the entry's creation date pre-dates go-live.
Sample 10 changes that answered no and independently confirm from the design document that they truly touch no NPFI.
List every go-live without a pre-dated entry and name the approver who released it.
testing.done: every NPFI-touching go-live traces to a register entry created before go-live, and mis-answered intake questions are named.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying the entry id or asset name, business area, data categories affected and the compliance impact.
Assign a root cause - asset never tagged, steward attested without review, intake question mis-answered, basis never sought, purge job not built - and an owner.
Set a remediation date, and where processing has no lawful basis require the flow suspended until it does.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's completeness run as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where basis is absent, a suspension of the flow.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the unregistered-asset count, the attestation completion rate and the blank-basis count and compare each to its threshold.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the Internal Auditor, who owns no register entry and stewards no tested area, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any unlawful flow to the Data Governance Council and the Compliance Committee, then file the workpaper under the quarter.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, measured completeness and a governance reporting date is filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Triage every new engagement for NPFI and NPHI exposure
actions: Attach the privacy triage questions to the sourcing request: will the vendor receive, store or be able to access policyholder, claimant or applicant data, which categories, from which system, and from which jurisdictions.
Route any yes to Third-Party Risk before a supplier is shortlisted, and record the triage answer on the requisition.
Set the data tier - tier 1 for NPHI, bulk NPFI or systems access, tier 2 for limited or aggregated NPFI, tier 3 for none.
Block requisition approval where the triage is unanswered.
checklist.done: each requisition carries an answered triage, a data tier, and a Third-Party Risk referral where NPFI or NPHI is involved.

checklist.step: Run privacy and security due diligence proportionate to the tier
actions: Issue the security and privacy questionnaire and demand the vendor's current SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 certificate, its breach history and its subcontractor list.
For tier 1, read the SOC 2 complementary user entity controls and the exceptions section rather than the opinion page alone, and record any exception that touches confidentiality.
Ask where the data will be stored and processed, including any offshore location, and get it in writing.
Score the vendor and record open findings with agreed remediation dates before contracting proceeds.
checklist.done: the tier-appropriate diligence file is complete, SOC 2 exceptions are read and recorded, and hosting locations are confirmed in writing.

checklist.step: Select the mandatory clause set from the approved library
actions: Insert the privacy and data security exhibit containing: use limited strictly to the purpose the information was disclosed for, no onward disclosure without written consent, confidentiality surviving termination, and the express prohibition on using NPFI for the vendor's own marketing.
Add the security clauses - administrative, technical and physical safeguards, encryption in transit and at rest, access limited to personnel with a need, and annual control evidence.
Add incident clauses - notification to the company within 24 hours of a suspected incident, cooperation with investigation and regulatory notification, and the vendor bearing notification costs.
Add audit rights, subcontractor approval, and return-or-destruction with a certificate within 30 days of termination.
checklist.done: the exhibit carries the full mandatory clause set drawn from the current library version, with the library version recorded on the contract.

checklist.step: Tailor for joint marketing and for health information
actions: For a joint-marketing arrangement, add the clause that the partner may use the NPFI only for the jointly offered product and must not resell, append or retain it after the campaign.
Where NPHI is involved, require an executed authorization from each individual before disclosure and prohibit any use outside the authorization's stated scope.
Where the vendor is an insurance-support organisation, add the redisclosure limits so information cannot be recycled into its own products.
Note the applicable exception on the contract cover sheet so the register entry and the contract cite the same basis.
checklist.done: joint-marketing, NPHI and insurance-support-organisation variants are applied and the contract cover sheet cites the same exception as the register.

checklist.step: Negotiate deviations through a controlled ladder
actions: Log every vendor pushback against a mandatory clause with the exact redline text and the vendor's stated reason.
Take use-limitation, onward-disclosure and incident-notification clauses as non-negotiable; anything else goes to Privacy Counsel with a proposed compensating control.
Escalate any surviving deviation to the General Counsel for written approval before signature, with the residual risk stated.
Record the approved deviation and its expiry on the contract record so it is revisited at renewal.
checklist.done: every deviation is redlined, risk-assessed, approved in writing by the General Counsel and given an expiry date.

checklist.step: Execute before a single record moves
actions: Route the agreement and privacy exhibit for signature by an authorised signatory of both parties and capture the completed certificate of completion.
Set the vendor record to 'privacy cleared' only when the executed exhibit is attached, and keep the outbound interface disabled until then.
File the executed agreement in the CLM with the effective date, renewal date, data tier and clause library version indexed.
Notify the sponsoring business area in writing that data transfer is permitted from the execution date, not the handshake date.
checklist.done: the exhibit is executed and filed, the vendor is marked privacy cleared, and the interface stays disabled until that flag is set.

checklist.step: Enable the data flow under the minimum-necessary rule
actions: Build the interface to send only the fields the contracted purpose requires, and hold the agreed field list on the interface specification.
Mask or tokenise identifiers the vendor does not need - full government id, full account number - and encrypt the channel with TLS 1.2 or better.
Join the extract to the opt-out suppression flag so customers who opted out never reach the vendor.
Have Third-Party Risk sign the field list off against the contracted purpose before the interface is enabled.
checklist.done: the interface carries only the signed-off field list, masks what the vendor does not need and filters on the suppression flag.

checklist.step: Control subcontractors and offshore locations
actions: Require the vendor to keep its subcontractor list current and to seek written approval before adding one that touches NPFI.
Check each named subcontractor against the sanctions and adverse media screen and record the result.
For offshore locations, confirm the safeguard on file and that the location matches what the register entry says.
Treat an unapproved subcontractor discovery as a contract breach: instruct removal or approve it retrospectively in writing, and log it either way.
checklist.done: the subcontractor list is current, screened and approved, with unapproved additions logged as breaches and resolved in writing.

checklist.step: Monitor the vendor's controls through the year
actions: Collect the annual SOC 2 or ISO certificate on its issue date and read the exceptions, not just the opinion.
Run the annual reassessment questionnaire for tier 1 vendors and the biennial one for tier 2, and compare answers to last cycle.
For material vendors exercise the audit right at least once in the contract term and document what was inspected.
Raise a finding with a remediation date for any control gap and track it to closure.
checklist.done: current control evidence exists for every tier 1 and tier 2 vendor with findings tracked to closure and audit rights exercised on material vendors.

checklist.step: Keep the vendor register and the processing register aligned
actions: Match every vendor receiving NPFI to a processing register entry naming that vendor as a recipient.
Compare the contracted purpose to the register's stated purpose and resolve any difference with the business owner.
Confirm the privacy notice describes the category of third party the vendor falls into.
List vendors present in accounts payable with a data-handling service description but absent from the register for triage.
checklist.done: every NPFI vendor ties to a register entry with a matching purpose, and payable-only vendors are triaged.

checklist.step: Handle vendor incidents against the contract clock
actions: Open an incident the moment a vendor reports a suspected event and record whether the report arrived inside the contracted 24-hour window.
Demand the affected record count, data categories and jurisdictions from the vendor in writing within 72 hours.
Assess the company's own regulatory notification duties from that data and hand the assessment to the Privacy Officer.
Log any late vendor notification as a contract breach and feed it into the next reassessment score.
checklist.done: vendor incidents are logged against the 24-hour clock with record counts obtained and late reports logged as contract breaches.

checklist.step: Renew or exit on the contract calendar
actions: Work the T-120 renewal alert: confirm the exhibit reflects the current clause library and refresh it where the library moved.
Re-run the diligence and re-tier the vendor if the data scope changed since signature.
Where the vendor is exiting, disable the interface on the termination date and issue the deletion or return instruction the same day.
Chase the destruction certificate and file it within 30 days of termination; escalate to the General Counsel if it is not produced.
checklist.done: each renewal refreshes the exhibit to the current library and each exit disables the flow and produces a filed destruction certificate within 30 days.

checklist.step: Publish the vendor privacy position to governance
actions: Report quarterly on vendors by tier, contracts missing an executed exhibit, deviations outstanding, overdue reassessments and open vendor incidents.
Show the trend so a growing tail of unassessed tier 2 vendors is visible.
Name the accountable business sponsor against each red vendor.
Table the report to the Compliance Committee and record the actions agreed.
checklist.done: a quarterly vendor privacy report with named sponsors is tabled at the Compliance Committee and its actions minuted.

checklist.step: File the contract evidence under retention
actions: File per vendor: the executed agreement and privacy exhibit, the diligence file, control evidence, approved deviations, subcontractor approvals and the destruction certificate.
Apply the seven-years-from-termination retention label and index by vendor name, data tier and contract number.
Confirm the file is retrievable by vendor name and by data category for an examiner request.
Spot-check five vendor files a quarter for a missing exhibit or diligence artefact.
checklist.done: each vendor file is complete, retention-labelled and proven retrievable by vendor name and data category.

checklist.step: Log and remediate vendor privacy exceptions
actions: Raise an exception for each vendor receiving data without an executed exhibit, each missing mandatory clause, each undisclosed subcontractor and each overdue reassessment.
Record the vendor, data categories exposed, root cause and an accountable owner with a remediation date.
Suspend the data flow where the exhibit is unexecuted unless the General Counsel signs a written, time-boxed exception.
Retest every remediated exception in the following quarter's sweep.
checklist.done: every vendor exception has an owner, root cause, remediation date, a suspended flow or a signed time-boxed exception, and a retest.

testing.step: Build the population of vendors that touch NPFI
actions: Extract every active vendor flagged as receiving NPFI or NPHI from the vendor register with tier, contract number and last reassessment date.
Extract separately the live outbound data interfaces and the accounts payable vendor list filtered to data-handling service categories.
Reconcile the three sources and treat any interface or paid data-handling vendor absent from the register as a completeness failure.
Have the extractor sign the reconciled population and record the queries in the workpaper.
testing.done: the vendor population is reconciled to live interfaces and payable spend with unmatched vendors listed as completeness failures.

testing.step: Reconcile every vendor to an executed contract in the CLM
actions: Match each population vendor to a contract record and confirm an executed privacy exhibit is attached, not just a master agreement.
Compare the exhibit execution date to the first data transfer date on the interface log.
List vendors with no exhibit, and any where data moved before execution, as automatic exceptions.
Quantify the records transferred pre-execution so exposure is measurable, not anecdotal.
testing.done: every vendor ties to an executed exhibit that pre-dates first transfer, or is listed as an exception with the pre-execution record count.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of tier 1 vendors, all joint-marketing partners and every vendor with an approved clause deviation.
Take 20 further vendors at random with a recorded seed from tiers 2 and 3.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every prior-quarter open vendor exception as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample covers all tier 1, joint-marketing and deviated vendors and is reproducible from a recorded seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the clause map on each sampled contract
actions: Read each sampled exhibit against the mandatory clause checklist and mark each clause present, absent or weakened.
Confirm the use-limitation clause actually restricts use to the purpose the information was disclosed for, in those terms - a generic confidentiality clause does not satisfy the exception.
Check the incident notification window, audit right, subcontractor approval and return-or-destruction obligation are all present with hard timeframes.
Confirm any weakened clause carries a General Counsel approval that pre-dates execution.
testing.done: each sampled exhibit has a completed clause map with weakened clauses tied to a pre-dated General Counsel approval.

testing.step: Test the data actually sent against the contracted purpose
actions: For 10 sampled vendors pull the current interface field list and the last transmitted file layout.
Compare the fields sent to the signed-off field list and the contracted purpose and flag every field beyond the purpose.
Confirm masking or tokenisation is applied where the field list requires it and that the transport was encrypted.
Confirm the extract joined to the opt-out suppression flag by re-running the filter against the opt-out population.
testing.done: the fields actually sent match the signed-off list, masking is applied, and opt-out suppression is proven on re-run.

testing.step: Verify due diligence currency and subcontractor disclosure
actions: For each sampled vendor confirm a current SOC 2 Type II or ISO certificate is on file and read the exceptions section.
Recompute the reassessment due date from the contract anniversary and compare it to the last completed reassessment.
Compare the subcontractor list on file to the vendor's current published list or last questionnaire answer and flag additions never approved.
Confirm any offshore location on file matches the register entry and has an executed safeguard.
testing.done: diligence currency, reassessment timing, subcontractor disclosure and offshore safeguards are verified per sampled vendor.

testing.step: Test the termination and destruction control
actions: List every vendor terminated in the last four quarters that had received NPFI.
Recompute the certificate due date as termination plus 30 days and compare to the certificate date on file.
Confirm the interface and the vendor's system access were both disabled on the termination date by reading the access and interface logs.
Treat a missing certificate or live access after termination as a fail with the data still at the vendor quantified.
testing.done: every terminated NPFI vendor has a timely destruction certificate and proven disabled access, or the residual exposure is quantified.

testing.step: Re-perform a vendor incident timeline
actions: Pick every vendor incident reported in the period and read the incident ticket and the vendor's written notification.
Recompute the elapsed hours from the vendor's detection time to its notification to the company against the contracted 24-hour window.
Confirm the record count, data categories and jurisdictions were obtained and passed to the Privacy Officer for the notification assessment.
Log any late vendor notification and check it was scored into the reassessment.
testing.done: each vendor incident has a recomputed notification timeline, obtained impact data and a scored consequence for lateness.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying vendor name, contract number, data categories, the clause or control that failed and the exposure.
Assign a root cause - triage skipped, exhibit not attached, interface enabled early, deviation unapproved, reassessment not issued - and an owner.
Set a remediation date and suspend the data flow for any vendor operating without an executed exhibit.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's sweep as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date, a suspended flow where required and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the unexecuted-exhibit count, clause coverage rate, undisclosed subcontractor count and tier 1 reassessment overdue rate against their thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references.
Have the Internal Auditor, who sits outside Procurement, Legal and every sampled sponsoring area, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any live unexecuted vendor to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper under the quarter.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, measured clause coverage and a committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Screening completed within 5 business days of initiative intake; full assessment drafted before the design freeze; approval recorded before go-live; high residual risk re-reviewed 90 days after launch and annually thereafter

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Initiatives that went live without a screening or an approved assessment, and mitigations closed without evidence, are logged with the initiative, data categories, residual risk and disposition

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero NPFI-touching go-lives without an approved assessment pre-dating release; 100% of high residual risks carrying a DPO signature; every mitigation marked complete supported by evidence - an unevidenced closure is a fail

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Assessment register export with initiative, data categories, jurisdictions, residual risk, mitigations and approver, with the underlying assessments behind it, producible to ALDOI within 10 business days
