checklist.step: Wire the screening trigger into initiative intake
actions: Add the privacy screening questions to project initiation and to the change record: new data collected, new recipient, new purpose, automated decisioning, offshore or new cloud region, retention change.
Route any yes to the Privacy Office within 5 business days of intake and stamp the screening id on the initiative record.
Block stage-gate approval where the screening id is missing.
Report monthly the initiatives that passed a stage gate without a screening id and who approved them.
checklist.done: every initiative carries an answered screening within 5 business days of intake and stage gates are blocked without a screening id.

checklist.step: Screen and decide whether a full assessment is required
actions: Read the screening answers against the trigger list and record the decision - full assessment required or not - with the reason on the screening record.
Mandate a full assessment automatically for NPHI, credit-based scoring, automated decisioning, offshore processing and any new nonaffiliated recipient.
Where no assessment is required, record which triggers were tested and found absent rather than a bare 'not applicable'.
Notify the Product Owner of the decision and the date the assessment must be drafted by.
checklist.done: each screening carries a reasoned decision naming the triggers tested, with the mandatory categories always escalated.

checklist.step: Describe the processing the initiative will actually create
actions: Write the data flow: what NPFI or NPHI is collected, from whom, through which channel, into which system, and who consumes it downstream.
State the purpose in the wording a consumer would read in the privacy notice, and name the recipients including any vendor.
State the volume - how many individuals and records per year - and the jurisdictions the individuals live in.
Attach the solution design and the interface specification as the source for these answers.
checklist.done: the assessment holds a source-backed data flow with purpose, recipients, volumes and jurisdictions.

checklist.step: Test the lawful basis and the notice position before design closes
actions: Decide whether the disclosure sits inside the service-provider, joint-marketing or transaction-processing exception, or needs an opt-out or an authorization, and cite the article.
Check the current privacy notice already describes this collection and sharing; where it does not, require a revised notice and set the earliest disclosure date at dispatch plus 30 days.
For NPHI, require an authorization design - form, scope, expiry and revocation route - before any build starts.
Record the basis on the assessment so the processing register entry can cite the same one.
checklist.done: the assessment names a cited basis, a notice position and, for NPHI, an authorization design before design freeze.

checklist.step: Rate the privacy risks against consumer impact
actions: List the risks: excessive collection, unlawful disclosure, re-identification, inaccurate decisions, over-retention, unauthorised access and vendor leakage.
Rate each on likelihood and on consumer impact using the published scale, weighting NPHI and financial-account data at the top impact band.
State the inherent rating before controls and keep it visible so mitigation credit is auditable.
Have the Product Owner confirm the risk list is complete for the initiative as designed.
checklist.done: every listed risk has an inherent likelihood and consumer-impact rating on the published scale, confirmed by the Product Owner.

checklist.step: Apply data minimisation to the design
actions: Challenge every NPFI field in the design and remove any field with no named consumer and purpose.
Replace direct identifiers with tokens where downstream use does not need them, and pseudonymise analytics copies.
Set field-level encryption for account, payment and government id data at rest and TLS in transit.
Record the fields removed and the ones retained with their justification on the assessment.
checklist.done: the design carries only justified fields, with tokenisation and encryption decisions recorded field by field.

checklist.step: Design access, logging and retention into the build
actions: Define the roles that may see the NPFI, the entitlement each maps to, and the certification cycle they will sit in.
Require read logging on the NPFI tables so an access review or an incident can reconstruct who saw what.
Set the retention period and the purge job, with the trigger event named, before go-live rather than after.
Record the entitlement names and the purge job id on the assessment so they can be tested later.
checklist.done: named entitlements, read logging and a purge job with a trigger event are specified on the assessment before build completes.

checklist.step: Assess the model where automated decisioning is involved
actions: Register the model, its training data and its NPFI inputs, and state whether any input is a proxy for a protected characteristic.
Run and record the disparate-impact testing the market conduct standard expects, with the metric and the threshold used.
Define the adverse-action explanation the consumer will receive and where the reason codes come from.
Require the model owner to commit to a monitoring cadence and drift thresholds before approval.
checklist.done: the model is registered with NPFI inputs, disparate-impact results, an adverse-action explanation and a monitoring commitment.

checklist.step: Agree mitigations with owners and dates
actions: Turn each unacceptable inherent risk into a specific mitigation - remove the field, add the vendor clause, add the consent capture, shorten retention - never 'increase awareness'.
Name a single accountable owner and a date for each mitigation, and mark those that must complete before go-live.
Re-rate residual risk after mitigation and show the movement from inherent to residual.
Return anything still rated high to the design team rather than accepting it by default.
checklist.done: every unacceptable risk has a specific mitigation, an owner, a date, a pre-go-live flag where needed and a re-rated residual.

checklist.step: Approve the assessment and set the go-live gate
actions: Review the assessment, challenge the residual ratings and either approve, approve with conditions or reject.
Sign personally any residual risk rated high and record the business justification and the accepting executive.
Write the assessment id back to the change ticket and set the release gate so deployment is blocked until pre-go-live mitigations are evidenced.
Set the post-launch re-review date at 90 days for high-risk initiatives.
checklist.done: the assessment is approved with the id on the change ticket, the release gate armed and a 90-day re-review scheduled for high risk.

checklist.step: Evidence the pre-go-live mitigations before release
actions: Collect evidence for each pre-go-live mitigation - the executed vendor exhibit, the deployed field masking, the consent screen screenshot, the purge job configuration.
Attach the evidence to the mitigation record; a status change without an artefact does not close it.
Have the Privacy Officer confirm each closure before the release board sits.
Escalate to the DPO any mitigation that will not close, with the option to defer the release or descope the data.
checklist.done: every pre-go-live mitigation is closed with an attached artefact and confirmed by the Privacy Officer before the release board.

checklist.step: Register the new processing on go-live
actions: Create or update the processing register entry within 30 days of go-live, citing the same basis the assessment recorded.
Link the register entry to the assessment id and to the vendor contract where a new recipient was added.
Confirm the privacy notice text in force covers the new sharing, or that the revised notice was dispatched with its 30-day gate observed.
Confirm the classification tags were applied to the new columns in the catalog.
checklist.done: the register entry exists within 30 days of go-live, cites the assessment basis and reconciles to the notice and the catalog tags.

checklist.step: Re-review high-risk processing after launch
actions: At 90 days pull the actual volumes, recipients and access logs and compare them to what the assessment predicted.
Test whether any mitigation degraded - masking switched off, retention extended, a new consumer added quietly.
Re-rate residual risk on the observed reality and reopen mitigations where the rating moved up.
Set the annual re-review and record the outcome on the assessment record.
checklist.done: the 90-day re-review compares predicted to actual processing, re-rates residual risk and books the annual review.

checklist.step: Report assessment coverage and open risk to governance
actions: Publish quarterly: initiatives screened, assessments completed, go-lives without an approved assessment, open high residual risks and overdue mitigations.
Show ageing on open mitigations with the accountable owner named.
Highlight any accepted high residual risk to the Compliance Committee by name and business justification.
Record the actions agreed and carry them into the next quarter's report.
checklist.done: a quarterly coverage and open-risk report with named owners is tabled at the Compliance Committee and its actions minuted.

checklist.step: Log and remediate assessment exceptions
actions: Raise an exception for each go-live with no approved assessment, each unevidenced mitigation closure and each overdue post-launch review.
Record the initiative, data categories, individuals affected, root cause and an accountable owner.
Require a retrospective assessment signed by the DPO within 20 business days for any processing that launched without one, and descope the data where the assessment fails.
Retest each remediated exception in the following quarter.
checklist.done: every exception has an owner, root cause, a DPO-signed retrospective assessment where processing launched early, and a retest.

testing.step: Build the population of NPFI-touching go-lives
actions: Extract every change and release deployed in the quarter with its initiative, sponsor and go-live date.
Filter to those touching NPFI or NPHI using the intake answers, the model inventory and new catalog assets tagged in the quarter.
Reconcile the filtered list to the project portfolio's delivered initiatives so nothing delivered outside the change process is missed.
Have the extractor sign the population and record the queries and run date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the go-live population is built from change, portfolio and catalog sources, reconciled and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile go-lives to screenings and approved assessments
actions: Match each population item to a screening record and, where triggered, to an approved assessment.
Compare the assessment approval date to the go-live date and list every approval that post-dates release.
List items with no screening at all as automatic exceptions with the sponsor named.
Quantify the individuals whose data was processed under an unassessed change.
testing.done: every go-live matches a screening and a pre-dated approval, or is an exception with the affected individual count.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of initiatives rated high residual risk, all NPHI initiatives and all automated-decisioning models.
Take 15 further assessments at random with a recorded seed from the remainder.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every prior-quarter open assessment exception as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample covers all high-risk, NPHI and model initiatives and is reproducible from a recorded seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the screening decision on the sample
actions: Read each sampled initiative's design document and answer the screening questions yourself before reading the recorded screening.
Compare your answers to the recorded ones and treat any suppressed trigger as an exception even where a full assessment was done anyway.
For initiatives screened out, confirm from the design that no mandatory trigger was in fact present.
Capture the design extract you relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled screening has an independent re-answer with suppressed triggers named and design evidence captured.

testing.step: Re-perform the lawful basis and notice position
actions: For each sampled assessment read the cited article of the state adoption and decide independently whether it covers the disclosure as designed.
Compare the initiative's sharing to the privacy notice in force at go-live and check whether a revised notice was needed.
Where a revised notice was needed, confirm it was dispatched and that no data moved inside the 30-day opportunity.
Confirm NPHI initiatives have an authorization design that was actually implemented, not just described.
testing.done: each sampled basis is independently verified against the cited article, the notice in force and, for NPHI, the implemented authorization.

testing.step: Test mitigation closures against evidence in the live system
actions: For each sampled assessment list the mitigations marked complete and open the attached evidence.
Verify the mitigation in the live environment - inspect the masked field, the deployed consent screen, the executed vendor exhibit, the purge job schedule.
Treat any closure with no artefact, or an artefact that does not match production, as a failed closure.
Recompute how many pre-go-live mitigations were actually closed before the release date.
testing.done: every sampled mitigation closure is verified in production, with unevidenced or mismatched closures listed.

testing.step: Test access, logging and retention as built
actions: Pull the entitlements the assessment named and list who actually holds them today.
Compare the holder list to the roles the assessment approved and flag anyone outside them.
Confirm read logging is on for the NPFI tables by retrieving a sample of access events.
Recompute the purge due date from the stated trigger and query for records past it.
testing.done: entitlement holders, read logging and purge execution are tested against what the assessment specified.

testing.step: Verify the register and catalog caught up after go-live
actions: For each sampled go-live confirm a processing register entry exists and was created within 30 days of release.
Check the entry cites the same basis and the same recipients as the assessment, and flag any divergence.
Confirm the new columns carry the NPFI or NPHI classification tag in the catalog.
List any go-live where the register or the catalog never caught up.
testing.done: every sampled go-live has a timely register entry consistent with its assessment and correctly tagged catalog columns.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying initiative name, sponsor, data categories, individuals affected and the control that failed.
Assign a root cause - screening skipped, trigger suppressed, gate overridden, mitigation closed without evidence, register never updated - and an owner.
Set a remediation date and require a DPO-signed retrospective assessment where processing launched unassessed.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date, retrospective assessment where needed and a retest.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the unassessed go-live count, the DPO signature rate on high residual risks and the unevidenced-closure count against their thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references.
Have the Internal Auditor, who authored and approved none of the sampled assessments, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any live unassessed processing to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper under the quarter.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, measured coverage and a committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Detect and raise the incident with a fixed discovery timestamp
actions: Work the data-exposure detections - large outbound transfers, mass record reads on NPFI tables, mailbox auto-forward rules, misdirected file shares - and confirm the alert is real before escalating.
Raise the incident ticket with the alert id, the first detection timestamp in UTC and local time, the systems involved and the initial data categories suspected.
Add intake from the other routes: employee report, vendor notification, consumer complaint about receiving someone else's documents, and department referral.
Never overwrite the discovery timestamp later - the statutory clocks run from it.
checklist.done: an incident ticket exists with an immutable discovery timestamp, the source alert and the suspected data categories.

checklist.step: Triage severity and pull in the privacy track
actions: Set severity from the data categories and record count in play, treating any suspected NPFI or NPHI exposure as at least the level that mandates privacy involvement.
Page the Privacy Officer, Privacy Counsel and the Head of Compliance within one hour of that classification.
Open the parallel privacy workstream on the ticket with its own owner so scoping and notification do not wait on technical closure.
Record who was notified and when, because the department will ask.
checklist.done: severity is set, the privacy workstream is open with an owner, and the paging record shows names and times.

checklist.step: Contain and preserve before anything is rebuilt
actions: Isolate affected hosts, disable compromised credentials and revoke the sessions and tokens tied to them.
Preserve memory images, endpoint telemetry, mail transport logs and database audit logs before any reimaging, and hash the evidence.
Record every containment action with a timestamp and the person who took it on the incident timeline.
Confirm with the CISO before any action that would destroy evidence, including restoring a system from backup.
checklist.done: containment actions are timestamped, evidence is preserved and hashed, and no system was rebuilt before preservation.

checklist.step: Scope the data and build the affected-individual file
actions: Take the exposed objects - tables, files, mailboxes, documents - from forensics and map them to data categories using the processing register's system-to-category map.
Resolve the exposed records to individuals through the MDM hub, deduplicate, and produce a file with name, address, state of residence and the data elements exposed for each person.
Split the file by data element because state thresholds differ - government id, financial account number, health information and credentials each trigger differently.
Reconcile the individual count to the forensic record count and explain any difference in writing before the determination is made.
checklist.done: a deduplicated affected-individual file exists with state of residence and exposed elements per person, reconciled to the forensic count.

checklist.step: Perform and document the harm analysis
actions: Assess whether the information was actually acquired or viewed, whether it was encrypted with the key uncompromised, and whether it was recovered before use.
Apply each state's risk-of-harm standard - some permit no notice where harm is unlikely, others notify regardless - and record the conclusion per state.
Where the safe harbour for encrypted data is claimed, record the encryption standard and evidence that the key was not exposed.
Have the General Counsel sign any decision not to notify a state, with the reasoning on the file.
checklist.done: a per-state harm conclusion is documented, with encryption safe harbours evidenced and every no-notice decision signed by the General Counsel.

checklist.step: Make the determination and start the statutory clocks
actions: Record the determination date and time that a cybersecurity event or breach occurred - this is what starts the 72-hour commissioner clock.
Compute per jurisdiction the individual-notice due date from discovery plus the state's outer limit, and adopt the earliest across the affected states as the operating deadline.
Identify states whose resident count crosses the Attorney General or consumer reporting agency threshold and compute those due dates too.
Publish the deadline table on the incident ticket and lock it against edits without counsel approval.
checklist.done: the determination timestamp and a locked per-jurisdiction deadline table are on the ticket, with the earliest date adopted as the operating deadline.

checklist.step: Notify the insurance departments within 72 hours
actions: Complete each department's cybersecurity event report with the date of the event, how it was discovered, the period during which it occurred, the information compromised, the remediation, and the number of residents affected.
File with the domiciliary commissioner and every state adopting the data security model within 72 hours of determination, using the department's stated portal or reporting email.
Capture the submission confirmation, reference number and timestamp for each department on the ticket.
Commit to the ongoing-update obligation and diarise supplemental filings as the forensic picture changes.
checklist.done: every applicable department is filed with inside 72 hours of determination and each confirmation reference is captured on the ticket.

checklist.step: Draft the individual notice to each state's content rules
actions: Build the notice with the required elements: what happened, the date or date range, the data elements involved, what the company is doing, what the individual should do, and a contact number.

Add the state-specific mandatory content - the toll-free numbers and addresses of the consumer reporting agencies, the state Attorney General contact, and the fraud-alert and security-freeze rights where the state requires them.
Produce the substitute-notice package - email, website posting and statewide media - for any state where the individual count or cost crosses the substitute-notice threshold.
Have the General Counsel approve the final text before production.
checklist.done: state-compliant notice text with all mandatory elements and any substitute-notice package is approved in writing by the General Counsel.

checklist.step: Issue the individual notices inside the shortest applicable window
actions: Release the affected-individual file to the notification vendor with the per-state text mapping and the required in-home date.
Run address hygiene against the national change-of-address file first so notices reach current addresses.
Capture the mailing manifest, postmark date and per-record disposition, and re-mail returns to corrected addresses within 10 business days.
Where law enforcement requests delay, obtain the request in writing, record the officer and agency, and diarise the release date.
checklist.done: notices are postmarked inside the shortest applicable state window with a per-record manifest, returns re-mailed and any law-enforcement delay documented.

checklist.step: Notify Attorneys General, consumer reporting agencies and other regulators
actions: For each state where the resident count crosses the threshold - more than 1,000 residents in Alabama - file the Attorney General notice in that state's required form and window.
Notify the nationwide consumer reporting agencies where the state requires it for events over the statutory size, stating the timing and distribution of the individual notices.
Notify any other regulator with an interest - a health regulator for NPHI, a securities or banking regulator for an affiliate - after checking the overlap with counsel.
File every acknowledgement and reference number on the ticket.
checklist.done: every threshold-crossing Attorney General, consumer reporting agency and overlapping regulator notice is filed with acknowledgements captured.

checklist.step: Stand up the consumer response channel and remedy
actions: Open the dedicated toll-free line before the first notice lands, with a script cleared by Privacy Counsel and a fixed answer for what data was involved.
Enrol affected individuals in the offered credit monitoring or identity restoration where the decision or the state requires it, and record the enrolment code on the notice.
Track call volumes, themes and any allegation of actual harm daily and feed them to the incident owner.
Route every department complaint arising from the event straight to the complaints queue with the incident id attached.
checklist.done: the consumer line is live before the first notice arrives, remedies are enrolled and call themes are reported daily to the incident owner.

checklist.step: Run the vendor-caused event on the contract clock
actions: Record when the vendor detected the event and when it told the company, and compare that to the contracted 24-hour notification window.
Demand the vendor's affected-record file, forensic summary and remediation plan in writing, and do not rely on a verbal count.

Confirm with counsel who owns the individual notice - the company as the entity with the customer relationship in almost every case - and do not let the vendor notify in its own name without approval.
Log the vendor's lateness as a contract breach and feed it into the reassessment and any recovery of notification costs.
checklist.done: the vendor's notification timing is measured against the contract, its record file is obtained in writing and notice ownership is settled with counsel.

checklist.step: Close the incident with root cause and control changes
actions: Hold the post-incident review within 15 business days of containment with Security, Privacy, the system owner and any vendor.
Record the root cause, the control that failed and the control changes agreed, each with an owner and a date.
Feed the failure into the privacy assessment programme so similar processing is re-reviewed.
Report the event, the notifications made and the control changes to the Board risk committee at its next sitting.
checklist.done: a post-incident review within 15 business days produces an owned root cause, dated control changes and a Board risk committee report.

checklist.step: File the event evidence under retention
actions: File the incident ticket export, forensic report, affected-individual file, determination memo, harm analysis, notice text as sent, mailing manifest and every regulator acknowledgement.
Apply the seven-years-from-closure retention label and restrict access to the privacy and legal groups.
Index by incident id, event date, jurisdictions notified and data categories so an examiner request can be answered by jurisdiction.
Confirm the file is complete before the incident is allowed to move to closed.
checklist.done: the event file is complete, access-restricted, retention-labelled and indexed by jurisdiction before closure is permitted.

checklist.step: Log and remediate notification exceptions
actions: Raise an exception for every commissioner notice past 72 hours, every individual notice past its state limit and every incident closed without a harm analysis.
Record the incident id, jurisdictions, days late, individuals affected, root cause and an accountable owner.
Agree with the General Counsel whether a voluntary disclosure of the lateness accompanies the filing.
Retest the notification control at the next quarterly test and in the annual tabletop.
checklist.done: every late or missing notice has an exception with days late, jurisdictions, an owner and a counsel decision on voluntary disclosure.

testing.step: Build the incident population and prove nothing bypassed the process
actions: Extract every privacy and security incident raised in the quarter with discovery timestamp, severity, data categories and closure status.
Extract separately SIEM data-exfiltration and mass-read alerts, vendor notifications and consumer complaints alleging misdirected documents.
Match each alert, vendor notice and complaint to an incident ticket; anything unmatched is a completeness failure investigated before sampling.
Have the extractor sign the reconciled population and record the queries in the workpaper.
testing.done: the incident population reconciles to SIEM alerts, vendor notices and misdirection complaints with unmatched items investigated.

testing.step: Reconcile notifiable events to filings actually made
actions: List every incident where the harm analysis concluded notification was required, by jurisdiction.
Match each to a department submission confirmation, an Attorney General filing where the threshold was crossed, and a consumer notice mailing manifest.
List any required notification with no confirmation as an automatic exception naming the jurisdiction and individual count.
Cross-check department acknowledgements received against the filings the company believes it made.
testing.done: every notifiable jurisdiction ties to a filing confirmation or is listed as an exception with its individual count.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of incidents involving NPFI or NPHI, every notifiable event and every vendor-caused event.
Take 15 further non-notifiable privacy incidents at random with a recorded seed to test the harm analysis on close calls.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every prior-quarter open notification exception as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample covers all NPFI, notifiable and vendor events plus a random slice of close calls, reproducible from a recorded seed.

testing.step: Rebuild the incident timeline independently
actions: Reconstruct discovery from the earliest reliable signal - the SIEM alert, the vendor email, the complaint receipt - rather than the ticket creation time.
Compare your discovery timestamp to the one recorded and flag any incident where the recorded time is later than the earliest signal.
Rebuild containment, scoping and determination times from the underlying logs and artefacts.
Capture the log extracts you relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled incident has an independently rebuilt timeline with any late-recorded discovery timestamp flagged.

testing.step: Recompute the 72-hour and per-state day counts
actions: Recompute elapsed hours from the determination timestamp to each department submission timestamp and compare to 72 hours.

Recompute individual-notice elapsed days from your independent discovery timestamp to the postmark date and compare to each state's limit - 45 days for Alabama and Arizona, shorter where the affected population includes a 30-day state.
Recompute resident counts per state from the affected-individual file and test them against each Attorney General and consumer reporting agency threshold.
List every jurisdiction where the recomputed count exceeded the limit, with the overrun in days.
testing.done: all statutory clocks are independently recomputed per jurisdiction with overruns quantified in days.

testing.step: Re-perform the harm analysis on the close calls
actions: For each sampled no-notice decision read the forensic evidence and reach your own conclusion before reading the memo.
Test any encryption safe harbour claim against evidence of the algorithm used and that the key was not exposed.
Confirm the analysis was done per state rather than once for the largest state and applied everywhere.
Treat a no-notice decision with no General Counsel signature as a fail regardless of whether the conclusion was right.
testing.done: each no-notice decision has an independent conclusion, a tested encryption claim and a verified General Counsel signature.

testing.step: Test the affected-individual file for completeness and accuracy
actions: Re-derive the individual count from the forensic object list using the register's system-to-category map and compare to the file.
Trace 25 individuals from the file back to the exposed records and confirm the data elements listed match what was actually exposed.
Trace 10 exposed records forward and confirm the individual appears on the notice file with the right state of residence.
Investigate any difference over 1% between the forensic count and the notified count.
testing.done: the notified population is re-derived and traced in both directions, with differences over 1% investigated and explained.

testing.step: Inspect the notices as actually sent
actions: Pull the archived image of the notice as mailed for each sampled state and check it against that state's mandatory content list.
Confirm the consumer reporting agency contacts, Attorney General contact and fraud-alert or security-freeze rights appear where the state requires them.
Confirm the postmark date on the manifest matches the date the incident record claims and that returns were re-mailed within 10 business days.
Test that the dedicated toll-free number printed on the notice answers and gives the cleared script.
testing.done: each sampled state's notice is inspected against its content rules, its postmark verified and its printed helpline proven live.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying incident id, jurisdiction, individuals affected, days late and the element that failed.
Assign a root cause - alert not ticketed, discovery timestamp back-dated, scoping slow, deadline table wrong, vendor late - and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date and agree with the General Counsel whether the department is told about the lateness.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test and into the annual tabletop scenario.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a counsel decision on disclosing the lateness.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the 72-hour compliance rate, the individual-notice on-time rate and the count of incidents closed without a harm analysis against their thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references.
Have the Internal Auditor, who sits outside Security Operations and the Privacy Office and worked none of the sampled incidents, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any late statutory notice to the Compliance Committee and the Board risk committee, then file the workpaper under the quarter.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, measured on-time rates and a committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Define the in-scope population from access, not from headcount
actions: Extract every active employee, contractor and temporary worker with job code, business area, manager, start date and work location state.
Join to the entitlement feed and keep anyone holding access to policy admin, claims, billing, CRM, the contact centre desktop, the warehouse or the document repository.
Include non-employee workers such as agency temporary staff and offshore service centre users, because the obligation follows the access rather than the payroll.
Publish the population with a cut-off date to the Privacy Officer and to Learning & Development as the assignment basis.
checklist.done: the in-scope population is built from entitlements joined to HRIS, includes non-employees, and carries a published cut-off date.

checklist.step: Refresh the course content against what changed this year
actions: Update the content for the year's changes: amended state adoptions of Model 672, the current privacy notice wording, new opt-out routes and any new sharing arrangement.
Build in the year's real incident themes - misdirected correspondence, over-collection at quote, discussing a policy with the wrong household member - as worked examples.

Cover the specific rules staff must apply: verify identity before discussing a policy, do not use NPFI for marketing where the customer opted out, never email NPFI unencrypted, report a suspected incident the same day.
Route the draft to Privacy Counsel and record the approved content version.
checklist.done: the content reflects this year's regulatory changes and incident themes and carries a counsel-approved version number.

checklist.step: Build the role-specific modules
actions: Write the contact centre module around caller identity verification, what may be said to a spouse or agent, and how to capture an opt-out on the call.
Write the claims module around health information handling, authorizations, and disclosure limits to nonaffiliated adjusters and vendors.
Write the underwriting and distribution modules around consumer report use, adverse action notices and producer handling of applications.
Write the IT administrator module around privileged access to NPFI tables, read logging and evidence preservation in an incident.
checklist.done: each role family has a module built on its own real handling decisions, with the module map agreed with the Privacy Officer.

checklist.step: Map job codes to modules and load the assignment rules
actions: Map every HRIS job code to the core course plus the role modules it must take, and have the Privacy Officer approve the mapping.
Load the mapping as automatic assignment rules so a new hire or a job code change assigns the right curriculum without manual work.
Test the rules with 20 seeded job codes across the role families and confirm the right curriculum lands.
Set the annual assignment to open by 1 March with a 30 April due date and the new-joiner rule to 30 days from start.
checklist.done: job-code-driven assignment rules are loaded, tested on seeded codes and set to the 1 March / 30 April cycle.

checklist.step: Build the assessment and the attestation
actions: Write scenario questions that require a decision, not recall - who may be told about a claim, what to do with a misdirected document, whether a marketing list may include opted-out customers.
Set the pass mark at 80% with a maximum of two retakes before the manager is notified.
Attach the attestation that the learner has read the privacy standard, will apply it, and will report suspected incidents the same day.
Confirm the LMS records the score, the attempt count and the signed attestation against the learner record.
checklist.done: a scenario-based assessment with an 80% pass mark, retake limit and recorded signed attestation is live in the LMS.

checklist.step: Launch the annual cycle and communicate the deadline
actions: Open the assignment on 1 March and send the launch communication naming the 30 April due date and the consequence of non-completion.
Send each people leader a roster of their in-scope team members with due dates on launch day.
Publish the course in the languages and accessibility formats the workforce needs, including the offshore service centres.
Confirm assignment counts reconcile to the published in-scope population before the first reminder goes out.
checklist.done: the cycle opens on 1 March with leader rosters issued and assignment counts reconciled to the in-scope population.

checklist.step: Train new joiners before they touch NPFI
actions: Trigger the privacy curriculum from the hire and contractor onboarding events, with a due date of start plus 30 days.
Have the joiner complete the core module before their NPFI system access request is approved, and record the completion id on the access request.
Chase at day 20 and escalate at day 25 to the hiring manager with the access-revocation warning.
Report weekly the joiners past 30 days who still hold NPFI access.
checklist.done: every joiner is assigned on hire, completes the core module before NPFI access is approved, and overruns are reported weekly.

checklist.step: Reassign on role change and on returning from leave
actions: Catch job code changes and transfers in the HRIS feed and assign the new role modules within 60 days of the effective date.
Reassign the full curriculum to anyone returning from leave longer than 12 months before their access is reinstated.
Remove assignments for leavers so the completion denominator is not inflated by people who left.
Reconcile the assignment changes to the HRIS movement report each month.
checklist.done: role changes trigger new modules within 60 days, long-leave returners retrain before access, and leavers are removed from the denominator.

checklist.step: Run the completion chase to the due date
actions: Send learner reminders at 30, 14, 7 and 2 days out and a manager digest of incomplete direct reports every Monday from 14 days out.
From 1 May escalate remaining non-completers to the business area head weekly with names.
Publish a daily completion tracker by business area during the final two weeks.
Record the reason for each non-completion - long-term absence, system access issue, refusal - rather than a blank.
checklist.done: reminders and manager digests run to schedule and every remaining non-completer has a recorded reason after the due date.

checklist.step: Enforce the consequence for continued non-completion
actions: At 15 days past the due date, suspend NPFI system entitlements for anyone still incomplete and outside an approved absence.
Notify the individual and their leader in writing of the suspension and the route to restore access.
Where the Head of Compliance approves continued access, record the business justification, the compensating control and the review date.
Restore entitlements only on evidenced completion.
checklist.done: entitlements are suspended at 15 days overdue or covered by a signed, justified exception, and restored only on completion.

checklist.step: Deliver targeted remedial training after incidents and complaints
actions: Take the quarter's privacy incidents, department complaints and quality-monitoring failures and identify the handling behaviour behind each.
Assign remedial training to the individuals and, where the pattern is team-wide, to the whole team within 10 business days of the finding.
Feed the theme into next year's core content and into the contact centre coaching guide.
Track remedial completion separately so it is not lost inside the annual figure.
checklist.done: incident and complaint themes drive remedial assignments within 10 business days, tracked separately from the annual cycle.

checklist.step: Train the producer and third-party channel
actions: Publish the producer privacy module covering the notice they must hand over at application, opt-out capture and forwarding a consumer request within one business day.
Require an annual acknowledgement from each appointed agency principal and record it against the agency code.
Require contracted third parties handling NPFI to certify annually that their staff completed equivalent training, and file the certificate on the vendor record.
Chase agencies and vendors that have not acknowledged within 30 days of the request.
checklist.done: producer acknowledgements and vendor training certificates are collected annually against agency codes and vendor records.

checklist.step: Report completion and comprehension to governance
actions: Publish completion by business area, by role family and by location, against the 98% and 100% thresholds.
Report the assessment first-attempt pass rate and the questions most often failed, because a weak question area predicts the next incident.
Name the business area heads with outstanding non-completers.
Table the position at the Compliance Committee and record the actions agreed.
checklist.done: a completion and comprehension report with named area heads is tabled at the Compliance Committee and its actions minuted.

checklist.step: File the training evidence under retention
actions: Export the year's training register with individual, course version, completion date, score and attestation, and file it with the approved content package.
Apply the six-year retention label and keep leaver records so a past year's population can be reproduced for an examiner.
Index by individual, business area and course version so a market conduct request can be answered by name.
Test retrieval on five individuals including one leaver and record the result.
checklist.done: the training register and content package are filed, retention-labelled and proven retrievable by name including for leavers.

checklist.step: Log and remediate training exceptions
actions: Raise an exception for each in-scope individual never assigned, each non-completer past 30 April and each new joiner with NPFI access beyond 30 days untrained.
Record the business area, days overdue, whether NPFI access was held throughout, root cause and an accountable owner.
Confirm the remediation - completion or access suspension - and close only on evidence from the LMS or the IAM platform.
Retest every remediated exception in the following quarter's new-joiner test.
checklist.done: every training exception has an owner, root cause, an evidenced completion or access suspension, and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Build the in-scope population independently of the LMS
actions: Extract all active employees, contractors and temporary workers at the cycle cut-off with job code, business area, manager and start date.
Join independently to the IAM entitlement extract and keep everyone with access to an NPFI or NPHI system.
Reconcile the resulting headcount to the payroll and contingent-worker registers so no population is silently excluded.
Have the extractor sign the population and record the queries and run date in the workpaper.
testing.done: an independently built in-scope population is reconciled to payroll and contingent-worker registers and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to LMS assignment and completion
actions: Match every population record to an LMS assignment and list anyone in scope who was never assigned.
Compare completion dates to the 30 April due date and to the joiner's start plus 30 days where applicable.
List LMS completions for people absent from the population and investigate whether the population or the LMS is wrong.
Compute assignment coverage and completion rates against the 100% and 98% thresholds.
testing.done: assignment and completion are reconciled in both directions with unassigned staff named and rates computed against threshold.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of new joiners with NPFI access, everyone recorded as an approved exception, and every non-completer past the due date.
Take 40 further learners at random with a recorded seed, stratified across contact centre, claims, underwriting, distribution, IT and offshore locations.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every prior-cycle open training exception as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample covers all joiners, exceptions and non-completers plus a stratified random slice, reproducible from a recorded seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the curriculum assignment rule on the sample
actions: Take each sampled learner's job code and independently look up the modules the approved mapping requires before opening their LMS record.
Compare your expected curriculum to what was actually assigned and list any missing role module.
Check learners who changed job code in the cycle received the new module within 60 days of the effective date.
Capture the mapping row and the LMS transcript into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled learner's assigned curriculum is independently re-derived from the job code mapping with gaps named.

testing.step: Verify completion records and attestations are genuine
actions: Open each sampled learner's transcript and confirm the completion date, the assessment score against the 80% pass mark and the attempt count.
Confirm a signed attestation exists with the learner's identity and a date, not a bulk manager tick.
Investigate any completion recorded in less time than the course runtime, or any bulk completion loaded by an administrator.
List every administrator-applied completion with the administrator's name and the justification given.
testing.done: every sampled completion has a date, a passing score, an attempt count and an individual attestation, with administrator overrides named.

testing.step: Test the new-joiner access gate
actions: For every joiner in the cycle with NPFI access, compare the access grant date to the core module completion date.
Recompute start plus 30 days and list anyone who held access beyond that date without completing.
Confirm the access request record carries the completion id where the standard requires it.
Quantify the days of untrained NPFI access per individual so the exposure is measurable.
testing.done: every joiner's access grant is compared to their completion, with untrained access days quantified per individual.

testing.step: Test that the consequence was actually applied
actions: List everyone still incomplete at 15 days past the due date and check whether their NPFI entitlements were suspended.
Where access continued, confirm a Head of Compliance approval exists with a business justification, a compensating control and a review date.
Confirm restored entitlements post-date an evidenced completion rather than a promise.
Treat continued access with no signed approval as a control failure.
testing.done: suspension or a signed, justified approval exists for every overdue individual, and restorations post-date evidenced completions.

testing.step: Test content currency and comprehension
actions: Read the deployed course version against the current privacy notice, the year's Model 672 adoption changes and the incident themes it was meant to cover.
Confirm the version deployed on 1 March is the counsel-approved version and not a prior year's package.
Analyse assessment results for questions failed by more than 20% of learners and check whether those topics recurred as incidents.
Recommend content changes to the Privacy Officer for the next cycle with the failure data attached.
testing.done: the deployed version is confirmed as counsel-approved and current, and weak topics are identified from assessment data.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying the individual or cohort, business area, days overdue, whether NPFI access was held and the control that failed.
Assign a root cause - population feed missed the worker type, job code unmapped, joiner trigger not fired, suspension not executed, administrator bulk completion - and an owner.
Set a remediation date and require completion or access suspension evidenced from the LMS or IAM platform before closure.
Carry every open issue into the next quarterly new-joiner test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and an evidenced completion or suspension before closure.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute assignment coverage, completion at 30 April and 31 May, and the untrained-access day count against their thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references.
Have the Internal Auditor, who sits outside the Privacy Office and Learning & Development and administers no LMS record, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any untrained NPFI access to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper under the cycle year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, measured completion rates and a committee reporting date is filed in the repository.
